newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE RUBBER QUIET, JAPAN HOLIDAYS A DAMPENER.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE RUBBER QUIET, JAPAN HOLIDAYS A DAMPENER.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midday on Wednesday with most of the trade sitting on the sidelines, weighed down by the Obon holidays in Japan, dealers said.

"It's very quiet. We should be waiting for leads from Japan but most of them are away for their Obon holidays so I don't know if they will give us any kind of direction this afternoon," a dealer said.
Another dealer said they were also waiting to see if consumers would engage in their weekly buying programme for RSS3 and TSR20 rubber.
Most of the trade want to see if major consumers like Bridgestone, Goodyear and Michelin will come into the market. "We'll see if they come in later. They normally do," one dealer said.
A dealer said lingering concern over the region's weak currencies may also keep trading subdued.
At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 92.50-94.50 U.S. cents a kg from 93.50 cents.
